solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make a mistake and almost quit

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to quit is to leave, the phrasal verb 'go' plus 'off'

explanation.surface: Someone slips up at work and is tempted to walk out altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last F from GO OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder or err is the informal sense of this verb, a slangy synonym for slipping up.

clue.text: Drugs of unusual quality in the 60s?

definitions.meaning: slang for illegal drugs, a dealer's stash
1960s Liverpool slang meaning great or fab, as the Beatles used it

explanation.surface: A wry look at the extra-strong narcotics of the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both modern slang for narcotics and Sixties slang for excellent, so two senses meet.

clue.text: Slightly unwell — or, on reflection, extremely poorly

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word or is read backwards
extremely means at the extremes, taking the outer letters of poorly

explanation.surface: Someone describes being a bit under the weather, or, thinking again, really ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns OR into RO; 'extremely' takes P and Y from 'poorly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, feeling a bit off-colour or below par is a British colloquial sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Daughter comes in to take cap off, revealing untidy hair

indicators.note: comes in means the daughter's letter enters the middle of the other word

parts.note: to remove someone's top, their head, is to decapitate them

explanation.surface: A girl walks in and pulls off her hat, showing hair in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take cap off' is a grisly way of saying decapitate; 'comes in' puts D inside BEHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair left messy and sticking up after sleep is called by this informal name, a just-out-of-bed look.

clue.text: Plant in pound range with moss for replanting

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: replanting means arranging again, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: a plant in a pound shop's range, to be repotted with moss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is the currency, L, not a weight or an enclosure; 'for replanting' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical grass used in Asian cooking is a plant, the definition being its broad category.

clue.text: Good examples of electronic form used to fill lists

indicators.note: used to fill means placed inside the other word, packing its middle

parts.note: rolls are lists or registers of names
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a mode is a form or manner

explanation.surface: Sample electronic documents are used to fill in registers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to fill' is the container signal; 'form' means a mode or manner, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: People held up for others to copy are exemplars, so they serve as good examples.

clue.text: Don't start getaway, then vigorously attack victim

indicators.note: telling the word not to start means its first letter is left off

parts.note: a getaway is an escape
to go at someone is to attack them with vigour

explanation.surface: Advice to a would-be fugitive: skip the escape and just lay into whoever is in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' drops the first E of ESCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made to take the blame for others is a fall guy, a victim of unfair accusation.

clue.text: Flipping big city area taken over

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: wen is an old word for a large crowded city, as Cobbett's Great Wen for London

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint that a huge urban district has been seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses WEN plus A. The definition is 'over' in the sense 'do it over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over means doing it again from scratch, so the adverb matches afresh.

clue.text: Group erected storage unit to support a citadel

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces that support another go beneath it, so the A goes on top

parts.note: a crop can mean a batch or group, as a crop of new recruits

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: A team puts up a storeroom to prop up a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns SILO upwards to OLIS; 'to support' puts CROP and OLIS under A.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified hilltop of an ancient Greek city, most famously Athens, is a citadel.

clue.text: Soft and hairy hybrid shrub

indicators.note: a hybrid is a crossbreed, a mixed product, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A plant catalogue describes a soft, downy crossbred bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' mixes the letters of SOFT and HAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-flowering bush with bright yellow blooms, a garden shrub.

clue.text: Gutless slugger boxing current holder of title

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the current letter goes inside
gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of slugger

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cowardly heavy hitter is in the ring with the reigning champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' puts I inside S and R, the ends of 'slugger'. 'holder of title' is not the boxing champion but a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight bears an honorific form of address, so he holds a title.

clue.text: Great success as one blocking corruption

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, here lodged inside the other word

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone person standing against corruption is a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' places I inside ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge hit, as a show that is a scream, is informally called this, an idiom for a smash.

clue.text: Hot soup is incredibly acidic?

definitions.meaning: a Vietnamese noodle soup served hot
pH zero, the most acidic reading on the scale, written with the zero as a letter O

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a steaming soup is fiercely sour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads as pH 0, with zero shown by the letter O; the question mark flags that liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vietnamese broth with rice noodles is served hot, and a pH reading of zero marks extreme acidity.

clue.text: Bun is light, creamy at first, covered with fudge

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped in, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: to fudge something is to fake or falsify it
airy means light, insubstantial

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of creamy

explanation.surface: A bakery describes a light bun with cream on top and a fudge coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudge' is a verb, to falsify, not the sweet; 'covered with' is the container signal. This is a small British iced sponge cake, like a cupcake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small iced sponge cake baked in a paper case is commonly called a bun in Britain.

clue.text: Situation marked by no frenzied frolicking?

indicators.note: frolicking means romping about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a calm state where no one is wildly cavorting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges NO FRENZIED; the surface also describes the answer, a pal kept from romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided state where one party wants romance and the other only platonic company is a social situation.

clue.text: I meddle to begin with and step in direct

indicators.note: to begin with takes only the opening letter of meddle

parts.note: to mediate is to step in between disputing parties

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being a busybody who interferes from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to begin with' gives the M of 'meddle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with nothing in between, as a straight line of contact, is direct in the sense of unmediated.

clue.text: Sailors in team synch manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving about, so the letters are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Crew members on a team keep their movements synchronised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges TEAM and SYNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: People who sail pleasure boats or racing craft are sailors.

clue.text: Rider provides cover for US soldier around animals

indicators.note: providing cover means enclosing, so the rider's letters wrap around

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, as a postscript, PS

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A horseman shields an American serviceman as beasts close in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not a horseman but an addendum to a letter; 'around' is the reversal and 'provides cover for' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmyard swine are animals, the definition naming their broad class.

clue.text: Couple possessing too much information about songbirds

indicators.note: possessing means holding within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join
TMI is the texting abbreviation for too much information
C, from circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A pair overshare far too much about birdlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' is the container signal; 'about' gives C, from circa, rather than signalling anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Small chickadee-like birds of the tit family are songbirds.

clue.text: Overly large but useful computer interface

parts.note: too means excessively, overly
L is the abbreviation for large, on clothing labels
bar means except, but

explanation.surface: A review says a gadget's interface is too big but handy.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of icons on a screen offers quick commands, a convenient part of a program's interface.

clue.text: Strip bar with little reputation tackles the crux of adverse publicity

indicators.note: tackles means takes on or grips, so the bar's letters hold the rest inside

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar

indicators.note: the crux is the heart, so the middle letter of adverse is taken

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity

explanation.surface: A seedy strip club battles bad press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip bar' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Strip' is the definition. 'tackles' holds E (middle of 'adverse') and the publicity letters inside the seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of something is to take it away from them, to dispossess.

clue.text: Female nurse headed to give assistance

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse in Britain

indicators.note: headed means with the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A woman nurse went to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed' removes the first letter of AID.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as Enid Blyton, stands for a female in crossword convention.

clue.text: Failing strategies, lacking input from good studies

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the remaining letters are jumbled
lacking input from means the strategies are missing this contribution, so the letter is removed

explanation.surface: Plans collapse because good contributions are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking input from good' drops G from STRATEGIES; 'Failing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned written works examining a subject in depth are scholarly studies.

clue.text: Place to stay during the last part of autumn

parts.note: in means during, as in the morning

indicators.note: the last part of takes only the final letter of autumn

explanation.surface: Someone books lodgings for late autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or small hotel offers lodging to travellers, a place to stay.

clue.text: Qualifiers seeing some competitors fight back

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read backwards
some means part of, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: Players in qualifying rounds see rivals hit back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds SFI across 'competitorS FIght', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions or provisos that limit a statement are qualifiers, as in no buts about it.

clue.text: Zulu queen clutches a religious text

indicators.note: clutches means grips, so the letter is held inside

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An African queen holds a sacred book tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' puts Z inside ER, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament is a religious text.

clue.text: Become aware stuff brought about tense, messy affair

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: to sense is to become aware of
to ram is to stuff or cram
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone realises that what they caused is a tense, chaotic business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' reverses both words together, giving MAR ESNES.
explanation.definitionFit: A complicated, confused situation, or a hoax discovery, is idiomatically called this, a muddle.

clue.text: In the end, it's ordinary and very meh!

indicators.note: in the end takes the final letter of it's

parts.note: O is for ordinary, as in the old British O level
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A shrug of a verdict: in the end, it's average and very underwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordinary' looks like the definition but supplies O; the definition is 'meh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An unimpressed shrug of a word means mediocre, merely middling.

clue.text: European fashion college

parts.note: ton is high fashion, the fashionable set

explanation.surface: A European style of school.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English public school near Windsor is formally a college.

clue.text: Understand, principally, that worthiness isn't guaranteed

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Grasp, above all, that merit is no guarantee of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch on or grasp is informal British slang for comprehending.

clue.text: How many make up a Spanish soccer side at any time?

definitions.text: How many make up a Spanish soccer side
definitions.meaning: eleven players make a football team, and the Spanish for eleven is this word
ever, at some point, as in if ever

explanation.surface: A quiz question about the size of a Spanish football team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish number for eleven players, and an English adverb meaning ever, at one time.

clue.text: Love getting into vacations to travel somewhere in the Atlantic

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the letter joins the other word
to travel means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romance blossoms on holidays spent touring an Atlantic destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges VACATIONS and 'getting into' slips O in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian province on the Atlantic coast is a place in that ocean region.
